messages.subject_clean: installing rapache on mac osx - problems with apxs and make
messages.body_plain:
Hi SN,
there is one step in the README that you missed, that is probably causing your problems. You have to install librareq2 before installing rApache, and then later give ./configure the location to the apreq2-config in an additional flag when installing rApache afterwards as so:
    --with-apreq2-config=/path/to/apreq2-config
You have to install it manually from the folder /libapreq2 in the rApache-1.2.3 folder that you got when you unzipped your rApache download, there is another README for it.

The fact that your env variable gave that error might be because you probably have only the command-line version of Xcode installed, or do not have it installed at all. In the first case, i recommend installing the full version and slimming it down later, as the CLI-version has numerous shortcomings and will cause problems again and again. Sadly, OSX does not seem to care about some major bugs in it that you will find people complaining about on Stackoverflow again and again.
In the second case, you should know that you need to have Xcode installed for the installation to work.

Best regards,
Z

messages.subject: Re: rapache permission
messages.body_plain:
Hi bernard,
I avoided that problem in the following way: I added the user of the running Ubuntu session to the www-data group, then chowned everything in the server folder to [user]:www-data with rwx enabled for the group members (chmod 770 or similar. note that this might have to differ for some files iirc.). Now the files that R makes by for example the write() function have [user]:www-data rights and can be called by Apache in another instance.
Adding the user to www-data:
sudo adduser [user] www-data
Changing the permissions in the server folder:
sudo chown [user]:www-data

I suggest that the user running the Apache session does not have admin privileges, so he can't call sudo himself. Maybe have those activated during development but disable the privileges for security reasons when your project goes live.

Hope this helps!

Best regards
Z

Jeffrey,

Let me start with some bold opinions. I personally don't want a framework. I want scripts to return JSON, xls, CSV, or images. I want a very simple set of rules to give to an analyst so that they an write scripts that will work on the console,, RStudio, and in RApache. I generally want it to be hard for analysts that don't understand web apps to want to do something that would be bad in the eyes of a traditional web programmer (insecure, non-performant, etc. Maybe I'll one day want something  like NancyFX, but for now one script per method is fine.

So some suggestions that I can at least turn into github issues:
* Can plotting by default not go to the script folder? Even if that simply means it goes to a temp file and there is a builtin variable with the temp file name?
* Can there be a new Handler where the plotting device is set to spew out to the http response body, and STDOUT text be discarded? I think that means the response body would be cached until dev.off is called.
* Can there be a new directive called REvalOnRequest that behaves like REvalOnStartup, but runs before a script is run? This will be useful if people want to do exotic things with plotting (e.g memory mapped files).
* Can the default plot be a svg
* Can plotting a second graph when the output method is not a multipage tiff or pdf cause an error to appear in the http log?

I don't code a lot of C, but I can try my hand at the first request at least. That seems straight forward.

Thanks
Justin
